originality.rationale: The rank-two and polynomial conclusions are routine consequences of older general theorems once the standard dihedral noncommuting-graph structure is written down. Barrett--van der Holst--Loewy characterize all real graphs of minimum rank at most two by the form of the complement; both parity cases fit that characterization immediately. Boyer et al. Theorem 1 gives the \(N-2\) coefficient as the number of vertex pairs with distinct deleted neighborhoods, while the universal top coefficients are already fixed. Counting those pairs in the standard dihedral join/cocktail-party description gives exactly the assigned parity formulas and minimum-set types.

final_claim: For the noncommuting graph of \(D_{2n}\), \(n\ge3\), real symmetric minimum rank is two and \(Z=M=N-2\); the zero-forcing polynomial has only degrees \(N-2,N-1,N\), with leading coefficient \(n(n-1)\) for odd \(n\) and \(3n(n-2)/2\) for even \(n\), and the minimum sets are exactly the complements of the stated two-vertex types.
